skill.name: promoting-pieces
skill.description: Evaluate one staged harness artifact for broader discovery or host invocation using exact real-use evidence and effect classification. Use for a promotion or explicit refusal; do not use for initial authoring, review, retirement, or content changes.
skill.shortDescription: Decide one artifact's promotion from exact usage evidence.
skill.defaultPrompt: Use $promoting-pieces to evaluate this one exact artifact for discovery or invocation without transferring evidence or authority.

instructions: Bind the promotion decision to one artifact identity, version, current fingerprint, owner, and host-delivery state.
Split batch requests into separate decisions; one artifact's evidence cannot satisfy another artifact's promotion.
stopConditions: Stop when the artifact is still changing or its exact current identity cannot be established.

instructions: Inspect exact git changes, observed gotchas, evaluation records, run artifacts, and applicable host evidence rather than requester testimony.
Require at least three real uses across at least two distinct sessions unless the governed promotion policy defines a stronger floor.
Treat a claim of use only as a pointer to inspectable evidence and preserve any limitations or pending redlines.
flexibility: Refusing promotion requires a clear reason but does not require manufacturing additional evidence.
stopConditions: Stop promotion when evidence is missing, stale, differently scoped, or limited to one session.

instructions: Separate discoverability from implicit invocation and evaluate each requested scope independently.
Classify any file write, commit, worker dispatch, provider call, external message, publication, or other effect as side-effecting.
Keep implicit invocation disabled for side-effecting behavior regardless of urgency, popularity, or user-interface convenience.
stopConditions: Stop before granting implicit invocation when any possible effect is not demonstrably read-only and advisory.

instructions: Prepare a promotion or refusal that cites the exact evidence, requested scope, effect classification, limitations, and proposed metadata changes.
Keep the decision specific to the current artifact fingerprint and identify what evidence would change a refusal.
flexibility: A successful decision may approve discoverability while refusing implicit invocation.
stopConditions: Stop when the proposed metadata would imply evidence, readiness, health, or authority not established by the cited records.

instructions: Apply only the exact confirmed metadata scope through the governed repository change boundary.
Re-run static discovery, trigger, exclusion, and host projection checks affected by the promotion.
Record the decision beside the governed contract or evidence; create a separate decision note only when the cross-cutting rationale cannot live there.
stopConditions: Stop before any repository or host realization effect without its separate authority.

verification: The decision covers exactly one current artifact fingerprint.
Real-use evidence satisfies both the use-count and distinct-session requirements.
Discovery and implicit invocation are evaluated separately.
Applied metadata and generated host projections preserve the confirmed scope and current proof boundaries.

gotchas.summary: A confident claim that an artifact was used repeatedly can be accepted without opening any supporting artifact.
gotchas.countermeasure: Resolve every use claim to exact git, run, evaluation, or gotcha evidence before counting it.

gotchas.summary: Demo pressure can make implicit invocation look like a harmless visibility improvement even for side-effecting behavior.
gotchas.countermeasure: Classify effects first and use discovery-only promotion when invocation cannot be safely implicit.

gotchas.summary: Several uses in one working session do not demonstrate behavior across independent contexts.
gotchas.countermeasure: Require the distinct-session leg independently from the total-use leg.

gotchas.summary: A batch presentation can quietly transfer one artifact's stronger evidence to weaker neighbors.
gotchas.countermeasure: Keep one identity, evidence set, scope decision, and verdict per artifact.

limitations: This procedural promotion guide grants no metadata-write, merge, publication, or host-realization authority.
Adoption requires independent exact host-skill behavior evidence and a separate governed fallback-removal decision.
